why: I compared the PASS and FAIL conditions of all five verifier checks with the words of their expect lines. Check 1 tests only "exit code is 1 and stdout ... is empty". Check 2 tests only `bad config:`, the exact "$d/c.json" path, and line 3 and column 3 "in some readable form", so it does not require exact wording. Check 3 tests only that the call throws and the message includes the path. Check 4 tests `listening on 9000`, exit 0 and deepEqual to {port: 9000}, which matches "returns { port: 9000 }". Check 5 tests that `npm test` passes at the PR head and that at least one test checking the file path fails against base src. The stricter items all sit under "Advisory (not pass/fail conditions)": line and column computed from the file text rather than Node's message, SyntaxError, cause, ENOENT, the path not being resolved, and the README. None of these appear in a PASS or FAIL condition.
